questionText: Which sentence correctly uses the past perfect to show sequence?
options: A) By the time she arrived, the show had started.
B) By the time she arrived, the show started.
C) By the time she arrived, the show has started.
D) By the time she arrives, the show had started.
explanation: Had started is the past perfect, showing an event completed before another past event - H-A-D S-T-A-R-T-E-D.

questionText: Complete correctly: 'Scarcely had the meeting begun _____ the alarm sounded.'
options: A) when
B) than
C) then
D) before
explanation: Scarcely...when is the correct pairing - S-C-A-R-C-E-L-Y. No sooner pairs with than; scarcely pairs with when.

questionText: Which sentence uses a noun clause correctly?
options: A) What she said surprised everyone.
B) What she said, surprised everyone.
C) That what she said surprised everyone.
D) Her what she said surprised everyone.
explanation: What she said is a noun clause as the subject - N-O-U-N C-L-A-U-S-E. It functions as the subject of the sentence.

questionText: Identify the correctly formed sentence with an absolute phrase:
options: A) His work completed, he finally rested.
B) His work was completed, he finally rested.
C) Completing his work, he finally rested.
D) He completed his work and finally rested.
explanation: His work completed is an absolute phrase - A-B-S-O-L-U-T-E. It has its own subject and a past participle.

questionText: Which sentence avoids the dangling modifier error?
options: A) Having studied hard, she passed the exam.
B) Having studied hard, the exam was passed.
C) Having studied hard, the results were excellent.
D) Having studied hard, success came to her.
explanation: She is the correct subject matching the participial phrase - D-A-N-G-L-I-N-G. The modifier having studied must refer to the subject she.

questionText: Complete: 'Not only did she win the competition, _____ she set a new record.'
options: A) but also
B) but
C) and also
D) also
explanation: Not only...but also is the correct correlative pair - C-O-R-R-E-L-A-T-I-V-E. Both parts must be grammatically parallel.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a participle clause?
options: A) Exhausted by the heat, the runner stopped to rest.
B) Exhausted by the heat, the runner was made to stop.
C) The runner stopped exhausted by the heat.
D) The runner, exhausting in the heat, stopped.
explanation: Exhausted by the heat correctly refers to the runner - P-A-R-T-I-C-I-P-L-E. The participial phrase must modify the subject.

questionText: Complete: 'Were it not for his hard work, he _____ the project.'
options: A) would not have completed
B) would not complete
C) would not had completed
D) will not complete
explanation: Would not have completed is the conditional perfect - C-O-N-D-I-T-I-O-N-A-L. This is an inverted conditional without if.

questionText: Identify the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:
options: A) The quality of the products has improved.
B) The quality of the products have improved.
C) The quality of the products were improved.
D) The quality of the products are improved.
explanation: Has agrees with quality, not products - Q-U-A-L-I-T-Y. The verb agrees with the subject, not the noun in the prepositional phrase.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an adverb clause of reason?
options: A) Since she was sick, she stayed home.
B) Because she was sick but she stayed home.
C) She stayed home although she was sick.
D) She stayed home when she was sick.
explanation: Since she was sick correctly introduces a reason clause - S-I-N-C-E. Since and because introduce adverb clauses of reason.

questionText: Complete: 'Had she known the truth, she _____ differently.'
options: A) would have acted
B) would act
C) will have acted
D) would had acted
explanation: Would have acted is the correct apodosis for an inverted conditional - C-O-N-D-I-T-I-O-N-A-L. Had she known inverts if she had known.

questionText: Which sentence is formed using correct ellipsis?
options: A) He plays piano, and she guitar.
B) He plays piano, and she plays guitar too.
C) He plays piano, and she does play guitar.
D) He plays piano, and she does too guitar.
explanation: She guitar uses ellipsis to omit plays - E-L-L-I-P-S-I-S. The repeated verb is omitted in the second clause.

questionText: Identify the correctly punctuated complex sentence:
options: A) Although he tried his best, he failed.
B) Although, he tried his best, he failed.
C) Although he tried his best he failed.
D) He failed, although he tried his best,
explanation: A comma follows the introductory subordinate clause - C-O-M-M-A. Although he tried his best is the introductory clause.

questionText: Complete: 'It is high time they _____ action on climate change.'
options: A) took
B) take
C) have taken
D) will take
explanation: Took is the past tense used after it is high time - S-U-B-J-U-N-C-T-I-V-E. It is high time always uses a past tense verb.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a fronted adverbial?
options: A) Under no circumstances should you give up.
B) Under no circumstances you should give up.
C) Under no circumstances should give you up.
D) You should not give up under any circumstances.
explanation: Negative fronted adverbials trigger inversion - I-N-V-E-R-S-I-O-N. Under no circumstances requires should before the subject.

questionText: Complete: 'The government, as well as private companies, _____ responsible for infrastructure.'
options: A) is
B) are
C) were
D) have been
explanation: Is agrees with government, the main subject - G-O-V-E-R-N-M-E-N-T. As well as is a parenthetical addition, not a conjunction.

questionText: Which sentence uses the passive voice in the present perfect?
options: A) The report has been submitted.
B) The report was submitted.
C) The report is submitted.
D) The report had been submitted.
explanation: Has been submitted is the present perfect passive - P-R-E-S-E-N-T P-E-R-F-E-C-T. It uses has + been + past participle.

questionText: Complete: 'Provided that she _____ on time, she would be allowed in.'
options: A) arrived
B) arrives
C) would arrive
D) had arrived
explanation: Arrives is the simple present in a real conditional - P-R-O-V-I-D-E-D. Provided that uses the present tense for a real condition.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a cleft structure for emphasis?
options: A) It was the teacher who inspired her most.
B) The teacher who inspired her most it was.
C) It was the teacher inspired her most.
D) The teacher inspired her most, it was.
explanation: It was...who is the correct cleft structure - C-L-E-F-T. It emphasizes the teacher as the subject.

questionText: Complete: 'She had no sooner left _____ it started raining.'
options: A) than
B) when
C) then
D) after
explanation: No sooner...than is the correct pair - N-O S-O-O-N-E-R. No sooner pairs with than; scarcely pairs with when.

questionText: Which sentence uses a gerund phrase correctly as an object?
options: A) She enjoys reading challenging books.
B) She enjoys to read challenging books.
C) She enjoys read challenging books.
D) She enjoys for reading challenging books.
explanation: Reading is the gerund after enjoy - G-E-R-U-N-D. Enjoy is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive.

questionText: Complete: 'The more knowledge you acquire, _____ you become.'
options: A) the wiser
B) wiser
C) more wise
D) the more wiser
explanation: The more...the wiser is the double comparative - C-O-M-P-A-R-A-T-I-V-E. Both parts use the definite article.

questionText: Which sentence uses reported speech correctly for a question?
options: A) She asked where he was going.
B) She asked where was he going.
C) She asked that where he was going.
D) She asked where he is going.
explanation: Where he was going uses indirect question word order - R-E-P-O-R-T-E-D. No inversion in indirect questions.

questionText: Identify the correctly formed sentence using 'wish':
options: A) I wish I could speak Japanese.
B) I wish I can speak Japanese.
C) I wish I will speak Japanese.
D) I wish I am able to speak Japanese.
explanation: Could is the past modal used with wish for present desires - W-I-S-H. I wish + past form expresses an unreal present wish.

questionText: Complete: 'On no account _____ the password to anyone.'
options: A) should you give
B) you should give
C) you give
D) you gave
explanation: Should you give uses inversion after a negative fronted adverbial - I-N-V-E-R-S-I-O-N. On no account is a negative adverbial.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a conditional type 2?
options: A) If he studied harder, he would pass.
B) If he studied harder, he would have passed.
C) If he studies harder, he will pass.
D) If he had studied harder, he would pass.
explanation: If + past simple, would + infinitive is the type 2 conditional - C-O-N-D-I-T-I-O-N-A-L. It expresses an unreal present situation.

questionText: Complete: 'He refused to acknowledge that he _____ wrong.'
options: A) was
B) is
C) were
D) had been
explanation: Was is the backshifted past tense in reported speech - B-A-C-K-S-H-I-F-T. The original present tense shifts to past.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an appositive noun phrase?
options: A) Delhi, the capital of India, is a vibrant city.
B) Delhi the capital of India is a vibrant city.
C) Delhi, the capital of India is a vibrant city.
D) Delhi the capital of India, is a vibrant city.
explanation: Appositives are set off by commas on both sides - A-P-P-O-S-I-T-I-V-E. The capital of India identifies Delhi.

questionText: Complete: 'By next year, she _____ her degree.'
options: A) will have completed
B) will complete
C) would have completed
D) has completed
explanation: Will have completed is the future perfect - F-U-T-U-R-E P-E-R-F-E-C-T. By next year signals a completed future action.

questionText: Identify the sentence with correct use of comparative adjective:
options: A) This is more efficient than that.
B) This is more efficienter than that.
C) This is much efficient than that.
D) This is most efficient than that.
explanation: More efficient is the correct comparative - C-O-M-P-A-R-A-T-I-V-E. Long adjectives use more for comparison.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses an infinitive of purpose?
options: A) She went to the library to study.
B) She went to the library for studying.
C) She went to the library in order study.
D) She went to the library for to study.
explanation: To study is an infinitive of purpose - I-N-F-I-N-I-T-I-V-E. In order to is an alternative that means the same.

questionText: Complete: 'She is _____ talented _____ she could become a professional musician.'
options: A) so...that
B) such...that
C) too...that
D) very...that
explanation: So...that is used with adjectives - S-O...T-H-A-T. Such...that is used with nouns. She is so talented that...

questionText: Which sentence has correct subject-verb agreement with a collective noun?
options: A) The team is playing well.
B) The team are playing well.
C) Both A and B are correct depending on dialect
D) The team plays well in British English only
explanation: Both are correct - C-O-L-L-E-C-T-I-V-E N-O-U-N. American English prefers singular; British English allows plural for collective nouns.

questionText: Complete: 'The results were _____ better _____ we expected.'
options: A) much...than
B) more...that
C) much...that
D) most...than
explanation: Much better than is the correct intensified comparative - M-U-C-H. Much, far, and a lot intensify comparatives.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a relative clause with whose?
options: A) The student whose answer was correct received a prize.
B) The student who's answer was correct received a prize.
C) The student which answer was correct received a prize.
D) The student that answer was correct received a prize.
explanation: Whose is the relative possessive pronoun - W-H-O-S-E. Whose shows that the answer belongs to the student.

questionText: Complete: 'Despite being tired, she _____ to finish her assignment.'
options: A) managed
B) manages
C) managing
D) to manage
explanation: Managed is the simple past verb - M-A-N-A-G-E-D. Despite is followed by a gerund or noun, but the main clause uses the past tense.

questionText: Which sentence demonstrates correct use of mixed conditionals?
options: A) If she had studied harder, she would be a doctor now.
B) If she studied harder, she would be a doctor now.
C) If she had studied harder, she would have been a doctor.
D) If she studies harder, she will be a doctor.
explanation: If + past perfect, would + infinitive is the mixed conditional - M-I-X-E-D. It shows a past condition with a present result.

questionText: Complete: 'Neither she _____ her brother was aware of the plan.'
options: A) nor
B) or
C) and
D) but
explanation: Neither...nor is the correct correlative conjunction - N-E-I-T-H-E-R. Neither always pairs with nor.

questionText: Which sentence has a correctly placed only?
options: A) I only eat vegetables on Mondays.
B) Only I eat vegetables on Mondays.
C) I eat only vegetables on Mondays.
D) I eat vegetables only on Mondays.
explanation: Only directly before vegetables clarifies that just vegetables are eaten - O-N-L-Y. Position of only changes meaning.

questionText: Complete: 'It is essential that every student _____ the rules.'
options: A) know
B) knows
C) will know
D) has known
explanation: Know is the mandative subjunctive - S-U-B-J-U-N-C-T-I-V-E. After essential that, use the base form without s.

questionText: Which sentence uses an inversion for emphasis correctly?
options: A) Never before have I seen such dedication.
B) Never before I have seen such dedication.
C) Never before I saw such dedication.
D) Never before had I see such dedication.
explanation: Never before triggers auxiliary-subject inversion - N-E-V-E-R. Have I seen inverts the usual I have seen order.

questionText: Complete: 'She had hardly sat down _____ the doorbell rang.'
options: A) when
B) than
C) then
D) before
explanation: Hardly...when is the correct pair - H-A-R-D-L-Y. Like scarcely, hardly pairs with when.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a comparative adverb?
options: A) She runs more quickly than he does.
B) She runs more quick than he does.
C) She runs quicklier than he does.
D) She runs more quicker than he does.
explanation: More quickly is the correct comparative adverb - Q-U-I-C-K-L-Y. Adverbs ending in -ly use more for the comparative.

questionText: Complete: 'He suggested that we _____ the meeting to the next day.'
options: A) postpone
B) postponed
C) should postpone
D) Both A and C
explanation: Both postpone (subjunctive) and should postpone are correct - S-U-B-J-U-N-C-T-I-V-E. Both forms are used after verbs of suggestion.

questionText: Which sentence uses the future continuous correctly?
options: A) This time tomorrow, I will be sitting in the exam.
B) This time tomorrow, I will sit in the exam.
C) This time tomorrow, I shall sit in the exam.
D) This time tomorrow, I would be sitting in the exam.
explanation: Will be sitting is the future continuous - F-U-T-U-R-E C-O-N-T-I-N-U-O-U-S. It shows an action in progress at a future time.

questionText: Complete: 'Seldom _____ she missed a deadline in her career.'
options: A) has
B) have
C) does
D) had
explanation: Seldom has she missed triggers inversion - S-E-L-D-O-M. Seldom is a negative adverb that requires inversion.

questionText: Which sentence correctly uses a concessive clause?
options: A) Although the film was long, it was enjoyable.
B) Although the film was long but it was enjoyable.
C) Despite the film was long, it was enjoyable.
D) Though the film was long, but it was enjoyable.
explanation: Although...enjoyable uses the concessive clause correctly - A-L-T-H-O-U-G-H. Never pair although with but.

questionText: Complete: 'I would rather you _____ early tomorrow.'
options: A) came
B) come
C) have come
D) coming
explanation: Came is the past tense after would rather with a different subject - W-O-U-L-D R-A-T-H-E-R. Would rather you + past tense expresses a preference about someone else.

questionText: Which sentence uses reported speech correctly for an imperative?
options: A) She told him to leave immediately.
B) She told him leave immediately.
C) She said him to leave immediately.
D) She asked him that he leave immediately.
explanation: Told him to leave correctly reports an imperative - R-E-P-O-R-T-E-D S-P-E-E-C-H. Imperatives are reported with tell/ask + to infinitive.

questionText: Complete: 'The factory worker, _____ had worked there for thirty years, was given an award.'
options: A) who
B) which
C) that
D) whose
explanation: Who is the correct relative pronoun for people - R-E-L-A-T-I-V-E. Who refers to the factory worker.
